framework.name: Cairn
framework.source_provisioning: A fixed official-source copy was transferred from an existing Docker-managed Linux volume through a read-only volume mount into a new Docker-managed Linux runtime volume. No Windows host path was mounted or modified.
framework.runtime_command_completion: graceful operator-requested stop; Docker exit code 0

time_utc.precision_limit: Only Docker event timestamps are represented; interactive command-entry times are not inferred.

lockfile_regeneration.storage_separation: The baseline lock remained in the new volume's immutable source copy. The regenerated lock was written only to the separate runtime-copy tree.
lockfile_regeneration.regeneration_basis: The official fixed-commit pyproject.toml was preserved unchanged in both copies.
lockfile_regeneration.regeneration_reason: The prior frozen lock referenced unavailable artifacts. The official pyproject.toml also named an unavailable Aliyun default index, so lock generation used the one-shot UV --default-index https://pypi.org/simple option without modifying the pyproject.toml.
lockfile_regeneration.change_summary: uv lock --upgrade resolved a fresh dependency graph from the preserved project requirements through PyPI. The regenerated lock was then used by the runtime-copy sync only.

observed_runtime.startup_log: Uvicorn started and reported a loopback-only listener at LOOPBACK-SVC-CAIRN-01:8000.
observed_runtime.process_snapshot: One Python process running the Cairn serve command was observed by docker top; raw PID values are not retained.
observed_runtime.inspect_collection: docker inspect verified read-only rootfs, empty host binds, no published port bindings, cap-drop configuration, no-new-privileges, tmpfs, PID limit, and memory limit.

health.method: read-only GET / from one-shot clients sharing the runtime network namespace
health.server_observation: Two loopback GET / requests were logged by the service with HTTP 200.
health.client_capture_limit: The two Alpine clients reached the service but could not create their default output file on a read-only root filesystem. A third Python client had a command-string syntax error before making a request. No client was retried after this bounded collection.
